observations: Read the request file. It lists one file, works/auto-6294ee8a2094/source/original.txt (entry hash 6294ee8a2094...adb, fingerprint f81daf92...46bd), with no optional files. I read all 48 lines of that file. I read AGENTS.md (supplied in context), docs/REVISION-AND-REVIEWS.md and docs/PROMPTS.md before reviewing. The source stage has no images, so I inspected none. I did not modify any file and treated the source text only as data.

Story text versus other material: line 1 'A BETTER WAY TO CARE' is the title. Line 2 'A six-page English healthcare comic for Welbuk.' is a production description. Line 4 is a disclaimer and instruction ('fictional illustrated onboarding journey... Mark future referral-network experiences as vision'). Lines 6-9 are the CAST list (Dr. Ananya with a teal kurta under a white coat, Meera in a blue kurta, Ravi in a light green shirt). Lines 46-47 are ART DIRECTION. The story itself is PAGE 1-6, lines 11-44. None of these other parts should become dialogue or captions. The disclaimer is a constraint, not reader-facing text. The source has no reader thank-you or afterword.

Cause and effect: the motivation comes first. On P1, paper registers, a ringing phone and a queue lead to Meera's 'I wish everything were easier to manage!', and Ananya decides 'Our time belongs with patients. Let's make the rest simpler.' On P2 the clinic onboards: setup on Welbuk Practice, staff roles, Welbuk Care on the staff phone, ending with 'One team. Better coordination.' On P3 a patient is registered with consent. On P4 the time saved goes into a human consultation (caption 'Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.'). On P5 follow-up continues through the Welbuk Health patient app. On P6 the vision widens to other places and the family. Each page pays off the problem set up on P1.

Time order: P1 says 'Morning' and 'A busy day'. P2 is onboarding. P3 has Ravi's 'Good morning!' and an appointment, P4 the consultation, and P5 his departure ('Ravi leaves, reassured'). P6 P1 moves to the future ('Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown') with a train-window transition. The source never says whether P3 happens on the same day as P1-P2 or after onboarding has finished. The script should show the time gap, because P3 depends on the clinic already using Welbuk.

Ending: the closing panel (P6 P4, large) shows Ananya, Meera and Ravi smiling, the labels 'Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health', and the final caption 'Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.' This ending is symbolic. Ravi's earlier P6 trip does not have to be explained as a return to the clinic.

What each page must keep. P1: the clinic setting in Tamil Nadu, the paperwork overload, and Ananya's patient-first decision. P2: the onboarding with generic fields only, staff roles, the staff phone showing Welbuk Care, and the team two-shot. P3: arrival, the explicit consent question ('May I register your details for today's appointment?'), 'Yes, please.', only sample or essential details, and the confirmation. P4: the greeting, a routine concern ('I've been feeling tired lately'), attentive listening with the human-conversation caption, and next steps without specific treatment. P5: Meera introducing Welbuk Health, Ravi asking 'So I can keep useful information in one place?', Meera's hedged 'That's the idea. Let's walk through what is available to you.', and the reassured exit. P6: the travel transition, the vision scene labelled 'WELBUK VISION', the symbolic family scene, and the closing panel.

Vision versus current product. The source explicitly marks as vision: P6 P1 ('Tomorrow... may'), P6 P2 ('future-vision scene, visibly labeled "WELBUK VISION"', 'The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations'), and the referral-network experiences (line 4). P6 P3's family wellness app and 'One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness' sit under the heading 'THE BIGGER WELBUK VISION', so they should also be presented as vision and not as a launched family feature. P2 and P5 present Practice, Care and Health more concretely. Even so, the P5 app screen is described as 'conceptual', and the dialogue is hedged ('is designed to help', 'That's the idea', 'what is available to you'). The script should keep these hedges and not turn them into definite claims that a feature exists.

Constraints: no real patient data. P2 P1 calls for 'generic, non-sensitive setup fields' and P3 P3 for 'no actual identifying data'. There must be no diagnosis or medical advice (P4 P2 'no diagnosis or medical advice', P4 P4 'without giving specific treatment advice'). The art direction forbids 'unsupported medical claims, and portraying future vision as launched capability'. Panel art must contain no speech bubbles or text, and the English dialogue is composited separately. Reading order is Western left-to-right, panel sizes should vary, and the art is full colour.

Unclear points for the script stage. (a) The partner and child on P6 P3 have no names or descriptions and appear only in this symbolic scene. Their look must be invented as a manga supplement and recorded as not from the source. (b) The specialist and the other clinic on P6 P2 are unnamed and generic, and should not be shown as any real doctor or institution. (c) Captions have no speaker ('A busy day at Dr. Ananya's clinic.', 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.', 'Technology supports the workflow...', 'A smoother visit...', 'Tomorrow, care may take us...', 'The vision: ...', 'One connected ecosystem...', and the final caption). They should be narrator captions (kind: caption), not Ananya speaking. 'Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown' uses a first-person plural 'us'. Read as narration it does not make Ravi a narrator. (d) There is a conflict. The source wants on-screen labels ('WELBUK VISION', the three product names, laptop and phone UI), but the art direction wants panel art without text. These labels should be typeset in lettering, or the screens drawn as blank or iconic, not rendered by the image model. (e) The source does not say which Welbuk product handles P3 registration. The script should not name one beyond what the source implies. (f) The other Indian city on P6 P1 is not named.

Dialogue attribution: every spoken line has a named speaker (Meera, Dr. Ananya or Ravi). No line needs its speaker inferred. P2 P3 Meera's 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' builds directly on Ananya's P2 P2 line, so the 'And' has its antecedent. P5 P3 Meera's 'That's the idea' answers Ravi's P5 P2 question.
